data.title: What SoFi Technologies Bears Saw Before A 55% Drop
data.description:
If you only read SoFi Technologies’ headlines in 2026, the story looked upbeat. Record quarters. Rising guidance. New products across AI, crypto, and business banking. Investors who held SoFi Technologies from the start of the year are down 54.6%, including dividends. If you had been weighing a position back on 1 January, how could such strong reported progress line up with such a punishing outcome for anyone who bought and held?

SoFi Technologies has already moved. Pinpoint other ways to investigate the theme among 20 cryptocurrency and blockchain stocks.

The Two SoFi Technologies Stories Investors Were Arguing About

The shares cost US$26.18 at the start of the period. Anyone looking at SoFi Technologies then had to pick between two very different but plausible stories about what that price already assumed.

The bullish narrative saw digital banking and AI as a powerful engine, with a Fair Value of US$30, a price that would make sense if SoFi’s tech, AI use, and product range helped it capture outsized market share and structurally higher margins.

The more cautious view put Fair Value at US$21.28, a level that only worked if revenue grew 19.3% a year and margins edged to 18.6% in a world where competition, regulation and macro risks limited upside.

What The Results Changed For The SoFi Technologies Thesis

The clearest new fact was SoFi Technologies reporting Q3 2026 revenue of US$1.37b and net income of US$240.989m, with net margin at 17.6% versus 14.6% in Q3 2025. That combination of higher sales, higher profit, and a fatter margin leaned toward the bullish case that assumed stronger economics, even while short seller allegations and tech platform pressures stopped it from fully settling the debate.

The practical lesson is simple. When a story hinges on future profitability, do not just watch headline revenue or app downloads. Track whether net income and net margin move in the same direction as the growth story, and compare that shift with what the original thesis described as eventual earnings power.

What You Would Be Paying For In SoFi Technologies Today

With SoFi Technologies now trading at US$12.48, this Narrative’s Fair Value sits above the current price according to Yang_, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the Narrative. The argument rests on SoFi as a combined consumer super-app and behind-the-scenes software provider rather than a plain lender.

Yang_ frames the recent share price fall as a test of belief in that twin-engine model. A buyer today would need to judge whether SoFi can keep turning one customer relationship into multiple products while scaling its technology platform for other institutions.

"The core investment opportunity relies on a major market misunderstanding: The market values SoFi as a traditional lender, but it is actually transitioning into the "AWS of Fintech." Just as Amazon Web Services (AWS) provides the underlying cloud computing power for the internet, SoFi provides the underlying banking software for the digital economy."

Not everyone reads the same price the same way. → See the higher figure this Narrative lands on, and how it gets there

Looking Beyond SoFi Technologies

SoFi might have you focused on digital banking, credit, and lending. One step away, there is a different kind of financial engine.

Instead of chasing a bank charter, this business leans into payments. It runs a technology platform that lets people and merchants move money online and in person.

You see similar themes here. Users pay, send, and withdraw funds while the platform still relies on partner banks for the heavy regulatory lifting.

The twist is how it uses that lighter balance sheet. More cash can flow into buybacks and software projects rather than regulatory capital, which shapes where future value might show up.

data.title: Caliber Mining and Logistics' (NSE:CMLL) Profits Appear To Have Quality Issues
data.description:
Caliber Mining and Logistics Limited's (NSE:CMLL) healthy profit numbers didn't contain any surprises for investors. We think this is due to investors looking beyond the statutory profits and being concerned with what they see.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

A Closer Look At Caliber Mining and Logistics' Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Caliber Mining and Logistics has an accrual ratio of 0.48 for the year to September 2026. Statistically speaking, that's a real negative for future earnings. To wit, the company did not generate one whit of free cashflow in that time. In the last twelve months it actually had negative free cash flow, with an outflow of ₹7.0b despite its profit of ₹1.56b, mentioned above. We also note that Caliber Mining and Logistics' free cash flow was actually negative last year as well, so we could understand if shareholders were bothered by its outflow of ₹7.0b.

Our Take On Caliber Mining and Logistics' Profit Performance

data.title: Innovision's (NSE:INNOVISION) Anemic Earnings Might Be Worse Than You Think
data.description:
The market wasn't impressed with the soft earnings from Innovision Limited (NSE:INNOVISION) recently. We did some further digging and think they have a few more reasons to be concerned beyond the statutory profit.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

Zooming In On Innovision's Earnings

One key financial ratio used to measure how well a company converts its profit to free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio. In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. You could think of the accrual ratio from cashflow as the 'non-FCF profit ratio'.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Innovision has an accrual ratio of 0.53 for the year to September 2026. As a general rule, that bodes poorly for future profitability. To wit, the company did not generate one whit of free cashflow in that time. Over the last year it actually had negative free cash flow of ₹1.0b, in contrast to the aforementioned profit of ₹148.0m. We also note that Innovision's free cash flow was actually negative last year as well, so we could understand if shareholders were bothered by its outflow of ₹1.0b.

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of Innovision.

Our Take On Innovision's Profit Performance

As we discussed above, we think Innovision's earnings were not supported by free cash flow, which might concern some investors. As a result, we think it may well be the case that Innovision's underlying earnings power is lower than its statutory profit. But at least holders can take some solace from the 33% per annum growth in EPS for the last three. Of course, we've only just scratched the surface when it comes to analysing its earnings; one could also consider margins, forecast growth, and return on investment, among other factors.
